title: 3 Better Networking Questions
subtitle: Three questions to ask after someone replies to your LinkedIn message or agrees to a quick call.
fromVideo: From the video: what to ask when they say yes
intro: Do not send all three in your first DM. Start with a specific opener, wait for a reply, then ask one question that fits their experience. Listen to the answer before you choose a follow-up.

entries.title: What helped you get your first opportunity when you did not have much experience yet?
entries.lead: Use this with an intern, recent graduate, or anyone only a few steps ahead of you.
items: Listen for a person, program, project, class, or habit you can investigate.
A useful follow-up is: What do you think made the biggest difference?
Keep it about their path. Do not turn it into: Can you get me an internship?
entries.note: Why it works: their first step is recent enough to remember and realistic enough for you to use.

entries.title: What do beginners in your field usually misunderstand?
entries.lead: This gets the correction that rarely appears on a company website.
items: You learn which skills, classes, or job titles people overvalue or overlook.
A useful follow-up is: What does a beginner usually find out too late?
Write down the part that changes what you were planning to do.
entries.note: Why it works: you are asking for judgment from experience, not a fact you could search.

entries.title: If you were in my position, what would you do in the next 30 days?
entries.lead: Use this near the end of the conversation to turn advice into one next move.
items: Give them enough context first: your grade, your interest, and what you have already tried.
A useful follow-up is: If I did one thing this week, which would you pick?
Write down the exact action, not just the general topic.
entries.note: Why it works: a short time frame makes the answer specific and easier to act on.

entries.title: Follow up with proof that you listened
entries.lead: The best thank-you message shows that their answer changed what you did.
items: Write down one recommendation before you close the conversation.
Try it, research it, or make a first attempt within a week.
Then send: Hey Maria, thanks again. You mentioned X, so I tried Y. I appreciated the advice.
entries.note: Do not ask for another favor in the thank-you. Give the relationship room to grow.

rule.title: The pocket version
items: What helped you get your first opportunity?
What would you do in my position over the next 30 days?
Ask one question, listen, act on the answer, and follow up with what you did.

verifyNote: Written for LinkedIn conversations with interns, recent graduates, and early-career professionals. Adapt the details to the person you contacted.
